svg.title: What runs between a push and the new release serving
svg.desc: A push to main starts two workflows. The checks workflow runs three jobs against a throwaway Postgres: quality applies both migrators and then lints, checks formatting, type checks and runs unit and integration tests; the end-to-end job applies both migrators, seeds content and runs the Playwright suite, whose accessibility and compliance specs are release gates; the Terraform job checks formatting and validates the stack. The deploy workflow runs on a native arm64 runner because the instance is Graviton. It assumes a role over OIDC rather than using stored keys, builds and pushes the runtime image, then builds and pushes a second image from the same commit's migrate stage, which is a cache hit because the runtime build already exported the shared layers. It then sends one Systems Manager command carrying those two image references. On the box the deploy script pulls first so a failure changes nothing, brings Postgres up and waits for it to be healthy, runs the migrate container once, and only then brings the application up and waits on its health check. It probes the health route and then fetches a real page, because the health route runs one query and never renders React. Nothing downstream runs unless that command succeeded: the edge is invalidated only afterwards, and the last step fetches the health route through the public site URL.
